answer.rationale: Activation and onboarding completion are both down 4–6% QoQ. Memory_31 and memory_86 both show that simplification of signup/onboarding drives measurable lifts in activation and completion. Verifying these will confirm the magnitude and durability of those effects before running a standard experiment. Promotional_pricing is ruled out because memory_73 shows deep discounting caused 12-point churn rise at renewal, undermining long-term revenue. Referral_incentive worked well (memory_57) but addresses revenue quality, not the activation decline. Activation_messaging (memory_91) is a secondary lever. Enterprise_sales_assist addresses a different segment. Onboarding simplification directly targets both declining metrics and aligns with proven prior wins. A standard_experiment scope balances risk and learning; we avoid broad_rollout given the QoQ decline uncertainty, and small_guarded_test would waste the week's capacity if successful. The competitor's pricing pressure on SMB makes sustainable activation lift more valuable than discounting.
